response_text: Calling osYield in any handlers which are involved in context switching can cause problems. Firstly, calling it in any of the functions which are run after calling osYield can cause an infinite loop, resulting in stack corruption and risk of a hard fault. When osYield is called, it triggers SVC_Handler, which then calls SVC_Handler_Main, running the case which schedules PendSV_Handler which switches context. Therefore, if osYield is triggered in SVC_Handler, SVC_Handler_Main, or PendSV_Handler, it will run osYield again, resulting in an infinite loop. This infinite loop will keep adding to the stack, which will cause it to corrupt and potentially hard fault. However, if osYield is called in SysTick_Handler, it will not result in an infinite loop, but will have unwanted behavior. Since SysTick_Handler is not called when osYield is ran, there will be no infinite loop. However SysTick_Handler is called every 1ms, and is used as a counter to trigger a context switch if a thread runs for too long. So, if osYield is called in SysTick_Handler, it will cause the context to switch before the counter reaches 0, resulting in a premature context switch.\n
